newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Small country, big bucks - recent Dutch buys abroad.
newsitem.headline: Small country, big bucks - recent Dutch buys abroad.

text.p: Tuesday's takeover of U.S. life insurer Equitable of Iowa by financial services group ING is the latest -- and one of the largest -- of a recent string of foreign mega-buys by Dutch companies.
The deal, which values Equitable of Iowa at $2.2 billion, ranks second in terms of size only to insurer Aegon's $3.5 billion takeover of Providian Corp's insurance activities last December.
Following is a list of other key Dutch takeovers in order of size:
Nov 22 1996 - ABN AMRO buys Standard Federal Bancorp SFB.N of the United States for $1.95 billion.
Mar 28 1996 - Retailer Ahold buys Stop & Shop SHP.N of the U.S. for $1.8 billion.
Oct 1 1996 - Dutch PTT agrees 2.7 billion guilder ($1.6 billion) takeover of Australia's TNT TNT.AX.
Dec 20 1996 - Dutch/Belgian financial services group Fortis AGTBt.BR buys MeesPierson merchant bank from ABN AMRO for 2.5 billion guilders ($1.43 billion).
Feb 26 1996 - Photocopier maker Oce van der Grinten pays 900 million guilders ($552 million) for the printing arm of Germany's Siemens Nixdorf.
Feb 14 1996 - Home products giant Unilever bids 1.23 billion guilders for Helene Curtis Inc HC.N of the U.S.
Nov 4 1996 - Food retailer Ahold buys 50 percent of Brazilian supermarket chain Bompreco which has annual sales of $1.4 billion.
June 23 1997 - Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed- Elsevier buys U.S. publisher Chilton Business Group for $447 million.
June 3 1996 - Transport group Pakhoed buys U.S. chemical transport firm Univar UVX.N for $300 million.
